children: A joint venture between Singapore's ComfortDelGro and France's RATP Dev has won a $2.63 billion contract to operate and maintain the Copenhagen Metro in Denmark.
The consortium, KBH Metro Partner, was selected after a competitive international tender, ComfortDelGro said Monday.
The Copenhagen Metro in Denmark's capital runs 24 hours a day and throughout the year. In 2025, it carried 135 million passengers.
The contract covers the operation and maintenance of the fully automated network, including four lines, 44 stations and 43 kilometers of track, ComfortDelGro said.
The contract is expected to be signed in September 2026, with operations likely to commence in September 2027.
It will run for 12 years until 2039, with an option for an extension for another three years, the company said.
The latest contract marks ComfortDelGro's second rail operation in Scandinavia, after its earlier contract to operate and maintain the Stockholm Metro in Sweden.
Growing its international public transport portfolio remains a core part of the group's strategy, said ComfortDelGro chairman Mark Greaves.
Copenhagen marks another important step in expanding the company's presence in Scandinavia and building a more diversified and resilient business, he added.
